world.h: Probe suggests Alaska gas project may serve Russian intel
world.b: A ProPublica investigation found surveyors linked to Russian gas giant Novatek worked off Alaska's sensitive North Slope in 2025 and this year. An expert called such Russia-backed information gathering near US shores a direct challenge to sovereignty and security.
world.title: A Natural Gas Project Off Alaska’s Coast May Be a Russian Ploy for Intel on the Arctic

world.h: US skips UN human rights review for second year
world.b: The United States left an empty chair at the UN's universal periodic review in Geneva for a second straight year, the only member state ever to do so. The ACLU told journalists the administration continues to violate human rights.
world.title: U.S. boycotts U.N. human rights review for second year running

world.h: Russia, Ukraine and US negotiators meet in Abu Dhabi
world.b: The talks are the first three-way round since February, with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner mediating. European foreign ministers pressed Secretary of State Marco Rubio for a seat at the table.

national.h: Three charged in Iran-backed terror plots
national.b: Federal prosecutors in Manhattan accused three men of being Iran-supported operatives who plotted nearly 20 attacks on Jewish communities in Europe and the US, plus a planned assault on RAF Fairford in Britain. Only one is in custody.
national.title: U.S. charges 3 men with plotting terror attacks, including planned assault on UK airbase

national.h: Door-to-door shots slow measles in Amish country
national.b: In Chester County, Pennsylvania, health department supervisor Dale Weiser has spent months driving to Amish homes to vaccinate families against measles. Word of mouth has spread her phone number through the community almost as fast as the virus.

politics.h: Sanders, Slotkin won't back Schumer as leader
politics.b: Sen. Bernie Sanders said he will not support Chuck Schumer as Democratic leader in the new Congress, joined by Michigan's Elissa Slotkin in calling for a new generation of leadership. Several incoming Democratic senators have echoed the call.
politics.title: 'The time is now for change.' Bernie Sanders won't support Schumer for Senate Democratic leader

politics.h: Senate Republicans keep Thune as leader
politics.b: Senate Republicans reelected John Thune, unopposed, as their leader after three tense meetings over midterm losses that cost them at least seven seats. Wisconsin's Ron Johnson, who pushed to delay the vote, walked out as voting began.
politics.title: Senate Republicans vote to keep Thune as leader after election wipeout

politics.b: The Senate moved forward a bill that would speed permitting for clean and fossil fuel energy projects, shorten environmental reviews, limit court challenges and make data center owners pay for the power infrastructure they need. Trump urged lawmakers to back it.

At his first Pentagon press conference in nearly six months, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth called Rep. Thomas Massie's impeachment resolution "a stunt" and "sabotage," framing criticism of the Iran war as policy disagreements. The House may hold a procedural vote on the resolution Tuesday.

politics.h: House Republicans pick Jim Jordan as minority leader
politics.b: Ohio's Jim Jordan beat Steve Scalise 106-73 in a secret ballot to lead House Republicans in the next Congress. The Freedom Caucus co-founder inherits a historically small conference after last week's midterm losses and warned of coming Democratic oversight.
politics.title: House Republicans pick Ohio Rep. Jim Jordan to lead them in the minority

international.h: Lewis Hamilton visits Gaza's Rafah crossing
international.b: The Ferrari driver toured the Rafah border crossing with North Sinai's governor, greeting Egyptian Red Crescent staff and asking how often aid can enter Gaza.
international.title: F1 champion Lewis Hamilton visits Gaza border

international.h: David Walliams accused of grooming young women
international.b: An ITV News and Guardian investigation accused the children's author and former 'Little Britain' star of grooming. Walliams denied being a predator or breaking the law, and the BBC is reviewing all material featuring him.
international.title: UK children’s author David Walliams accused of grooming minors

international.b: Russia expelled a Moldovan diplomat in retaliation for Moldova's expulsion of a Russian embassy employee in October, after Moldova said a Russian drone carrying explosives crashed near homes and an energy facility.
international.title: Russia expels Moldovan diplomat in tit-for-tat move

international.h: UN peacekeepers come under fire in southern Lebanon
international.b: A UNIFIL patrol was shot at in southern Lebanon and returned fire. No casualties were reported, and the mission called for an investigation, warning that deliberate attacks on peacekeepers violate international law.
international.title: UNIFIL patrol comes under fire in southern Lebanon

international.h: Rwanda genocide suspect deported from US to face trial
international.b: Jean Léonard Teganya, indicted in 2014 over alleged genocide crimes in Huye district, arrived in Rwanda Monday after deportation from the United States and is being questioned by police before prosecutors take his case.

international.h: US soldier arrested in Britain on Russia spying suspicion
international.b: Counterterror police arrested a 41-year-old US soldier near Gloucester on suspicion of assisting a foreign intelligence service, working with the FBI and US military. FBI Director Kash Patel called it an important arrest.

international.h: Israel's president urges compromise as new Knesset sworn in
international.b: Israel's president urged lawmakers to make concessions and avoid a repeat election as the 26th Knesset was sworn in. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, tasked with forming a government, has 28 days to build a coalition.
international.title: Israeli president warns against repeat election in new Knesset session

international.h: Egypt train crash fuels calls for accountability
international.b: Parliament's transport committee summoned the transport minister after a Giza-Fayoum train rammed another on the Cairo-Aswan line Sunday in al-Ayyat district. Opposition voices are demanding resignations as the crash questions years of railway upgrades.

international.h: Indonesia's vice president offers to resign
international.b: Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka, son of former President Joko Widodo, offered to resign in a meeting with President Prabowo Subianto amid questions over his academic documents. It was not clear whether Prabowo accepted.
international.title: Indonesia's VP offers resignation as questions mount over his eligibility

international.h: Spain weighs suspending TikTok over abuse videos
international.b: Spain is considering suspending TikTok after the nonprofit Maldita.es found more than 1,000 child sexual abuse videos with 48 million views and over 20,000 suspected predator profiles during 35 days of monitoring.

international.h: Fog pile-up kills at least 12 in Bulgaria
international.b: About 50 cars and trucks crashed in thick fog on the motorway near Yambol linking Sofia and Burgas, killing at least 12 and sending 46 to hospital. Prime Minister Rumen Radev called it a tragedy.

international.h: Three workers die at Tata iPhone parts plant
international.b: Three contract workers died after inhaling gas while cleaning an effluent treatment tank at a Tata Electronics site in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, late Monday. Tata handles roughly 40% of iPhone assembly in India.

international.h: US moves aircraft from second UK base over Iran threat
international.b: US refuelling tankers at RAF Mildenhall in eastern England were diverted to Germany and elsewhere Monday after a threat from Iran, The Wall Street Journal reported. Mildenhall and RAF Lakenheath were raised to FPCON Charlie, the second-highest threat level.

international.h: Europe presses Rubio for a seat at Ukraine talks
international.b: Meeting in Paris with G7 counterparts, European foreign ministers told Secretary of State Marco Rubio that Europe must have a say in any deal to end Russia's war on Ukraine, as US-mediated talks began in Abu Dhabi. Germany's Johann Wadephul rejected any fundamental change to Europe's security architecture.

international.h: Israeli forces kill 14-year-old Palestinian in West Bank raid
international.b: Moataz Iyad Daghlas was shot in the village of Burqa near Nablus, and two other teens were wounded. Israel's military said soldiers fired to stop stone-throwing.

international.h: Saudi Arabia downs missiles fired at Riyadh
international.b: A Saudi-led coalition spokesperson blamed the Houthis after two ballistic missiles and a cruise missile were intercepted, following an attack on a key pipeline.

international.h: Cameroon sets Feb. 7 date for twice-delayed elections
international.b: President Paul Biya, 93, announced the legislative and local vote by decree as authorities crack down on the opposition a year after his disputed reelection.

business.h: IBM Consulting ends most US foreign worker sponsorships
business.b: IBM's biggest division, with more than 150,000 employees, will end most sponsorships of foreign workers in the US, saying its use of high-skilled visa programs had been declining for years. The move comes amid Trump administration pressure on H-1B use.
business.title: IBM’s biggest division ends most US foreign worker sponsorships

business.h: Anthropic targets $1.4 trillion valuation in IPO
business.b: Anthropic's SEC filing plans 825 million shares priced at $70 to $78, valuing the AI company at up to $1.4 trillion, plus a $26 billion private placement backed by Google, Nvidia, Microsoft and AMD. The valuation is below earlier estimates amid worries over AI spending.
business.title: Anthropic targets $1.4 trillion valuation in massive stock market debut

business.h: New car prices hit a record above $51,000
business.b: The average transaction price for a new vehicle reached $51,109, Kelley Blue Book reported, about $500 above the previous record. The 2.1% yearly rise is below inflation, as tariffs and demand for larger vehicles keep prices high.

business.h: Inflation runs hotter than expected in October
business.b: Consumer prices rose 0.4% from September to October and core prices rose 0.3%, both a tenth of a point above forecasts, the Labor Department said. At an annual rate both are well above the Fed's 2% target.

business.h: Gates holds $29 billion stake in landfill giant
business.b: A ProPublica investigation finds Bill Gates owns 38% of Republic Services, America's No. 2 landfill operator. EPA inspectors have repeatedly found methane escaping Republic landfills above federal limits, and the company has lobbied against rules that would make the waste industry cleaner.
business.title: Bill Gates Wants to Stop Global Warming. He’s Earned Billions From Climate-Polluting Landfills.

science.h: Iran war oil shock trims global CO2 emissions
science.b: Fossil fuel carbon emissions fell 0.4% in 2026 to 38.2 billion metric tons, the Global Carbon Project found, mostly because the Iran war choked oil through the Strait of Hormuz. Oil emissions dropped nearly 2% while coal rose 0.6%.

sports.b: Minnesota reacquired Kirk Cousins from the Raiders for a 2027 third-round pick ahead of the trade deadline, after Carson Wentz went 8-for-25 Monday. The deal hands Las Vegas's starting job to No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza.

sports.h: Kevin McGonigle and Sal Stewart win Rookie of the Year
sports.b: The Tigers' McGonigle took 28 of 30 first-place votes in the AL, and the Reds' Stewart won in the NL.

sports.h: Jaguars trade for Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis
sports.b: Jacksonville sent a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to Philadelphia on the eve of the trade deadline, after also adding Jessie Bates III and Davon Godchaux.

sports.h: College Football Playoff expanding to 24 teams in 2027
sports.b: The new format has 19 at-large bids, four for Power Four champions and one for the top Group of Six champion, and will eliminate conference championship games, CBS Sports reports.

sports.h: Jaguars acquire All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III from Falcons
sports.b: Atlanta gets a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Jacksonville is 6-2, and the NFL trade deadline is Tuesday.

goodnews.h: Norway's eider keepers build nests for migrating ducks
goodnews.b: On the Vega Islands, just south of the Arctic Circle, keepers shelter nesting eider ducks each spring and collect their prized down.

goodnews.h: Nations pledge to double rooftop solar by 2030
goodnews.b: At the COP31 climate talks in Turkey, five countries launched the Global Rooftop Solar Declaration, aiming to grow homes with rooftop panels from about 150 million to at least 300 million by 2030.

local.h: Ninth death in city jail custody this year
local.b: A man held at Rikers' Robert N. Davoren Center was found dead in his bed, at least the ninth death in Department of Correction custody this year. The department did not release a cause and will investigate.
local.title: Rikers detainee's death is at least the 9th in corrections department custody this year

local.h: Hochul keeps door open to redrawing House map
local.b: Gov. Kathy Hochul said Democratic gains don't necessarily end the push to amend the state constitution for mid-decade redistricting, which could let Democrats redraw New York's districts as soon as 2028, but she didn't commit.
local.title: Gov. Hochul keeps the door open to redrawing New York’s congressional map

local.h: Man indicted in killing of Brooklyn runner Katie Suarez
local.b: Brooklyn prosecutors indicted a city Department of Education worker in the Oct. 30 stabbing of Katie Suarez on a Bath Beach path. Police say surveillance shows him fleeing the scene.
local.title: Man indicted in stabbing murder of Brooklyn runner Katie Suarez

local.h: Judge orders city to answer ICE shelter subpoena
local.b: A federal judge ruled City Hall must give ICE the names and birthdates of South Bronx migrant shelter residents with serious criminal histories. The Mamdani administration says it is evaluating next steps.
local.title: ICE subpoena puts a spotlight on the last emergency migrant shelter in NYC

local.b: The city's Department of Transportation told a community board that concrete work on west Canal Street, planned for this fall, will slip to next year in the Reimagining Canal Street project.
local.title: Manhattan's Canal Street is getting a face-lift, but it'll take a while

local.h: East Harlem buildings head to auction despite City Hall push
local.b: Thirty-eight deteriorating buildings with about 850 mostly rent-stabilized apartments, formerly owned by bankrupt Emerald Equities Group, go to auction starting Tuesday. Mayor Mamdani's administration had backed a bid by affordable housing developer Spatial Equity to buy the portfolio first.
local.title: Rent-stabilized buildings hit auction block, despite Mamdani’s efforts to intervene

periods.text: Mostly sunny, with a high near 61. West wind around 6 mph.

periods.text: A 40 percent chance of rain after 1am.  Mostly cloudy, with a low around 53. Light and variable wind becoming east 5 to 7 mph after midnight.

periods.text: Rain.  High near 59. East wind 9 to 11 mph.  Chance of precipitation is 100%. New precipitation amounts between a quarter and half of an inch possible.

periods.name: Thursday Night
periods.text: Rain likely.  Mostly cloudy, with a low around 45. North wind 11 to 16 mph.  Chance of precipitation is 70%. New precipitation amounts between a quarter and half of an inch possible.

periods.name: Friday
periods.text: Rain.  High near 47. Chance of precipitation is 80%. New precipitation amounts between a tenth and quarter of an inch possible.
